Officially, he is here to restore order and keep the station operational. Unofficially, both the crew and Martin himself suspect there is more to his appointment than anyone is saying. # The Edge Station The Edge Station is isolated, overworked, politically compromised, and always one failure away from crisis. It exists to observe, survive, and exploit whatever can be learned from The Veil without letting The Veil consume everyone stationed there. The station is not a sleek utopia. It is a hard-working, aging, high-risk outpost where every department is under pressure: - engineering keeps old systems alive under constant strain - medical handles exposure risks, biological anomalies, and incomplete records - security balances internal trust with containment concerns - logistics rations finite supplies and replacement parts - science is constantly tempted to push too far - command is expected to hold everything together while knowing too little The station’s crew is highly competent, but not automatically unified. This policy began under the original **Veil Adaptation Program**, after early mixed-crew trials near The Veil produced unacceptable neurological, psychological, and biological failure rates. Later female-only crews showed better long-duration survival and operational stability, though the real reason remains disputed, classified, and politically sensitive.
